children: Twenty One Capital is shopping again. The Bitcoin-focused public company bought 172.25 BTC on November 20, 2026, for approximately $10 million.
That works out to an average of about $58,054 per Bitcoin. It brings the firm's total reported holdings to approximately 43,841 BTC.
It was the company's second buy in less than a week, and both arrived while the crypto market was getting knocked around.
The November 20 purchase followed another one on November 16. In that earlier deal, Twenty One Capital picked up 154.32 BTC, also for around $10 million.
The average price on that first buy was about $64,801 per coin. Four days later, the same budget bought more Bitcoin, at several thousand dollars less per coin.
According to the company's Q3 10-Q filing, Twenty One Capital held 43,514 BTC as of September 30, 2026.
Add the 154.32 BTC from November 16 and the 172.25 BTC from November 20, and you land at roughly 43,841 BTC. Combined, the two purchases added a little over 326 coins to the treasury.
The roughly $20 million spent across both deals is a modest commitment for a company sitting on tens of thousands of Bitcoin.

Twenty One Capital, Inc. trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker XXI. It went public on December 9, 2025, after merging with Cantor Equity Partners, a special purpose acquisition company.
The company arrived on public markets already holding more than 43,500 BTC.

Its backers are well known in crypto circles. The company was co-founded by Tether, the issuer of the largest dollar-pegged stablecoin, and Jack Mallers, the entrepreneur known for building Bitcoin payments app Strike.
SoftBank was also involved early on. In 2026, Tether consolidated its control of the company by purchasing SoftBank's stake.
Twenty One Capital operates with approximately $102.8 million in cash.
It also carries approximately $486.5 million in convertible notes. Those notes are collateralized by approximately 16,116 BTC.

A convertible note is a loan that lenders can later swap for company stock instead of getting their cash back. Collateralized means a chunk of the Bitcoin is pledged as backing for that debt. So roughly 16,116 of the company's coins are tied up as security for those notes, which is a meaningful share of the total holdings.
With roughly 16,116 BTC backing about $486.5 million in convertible notes, falling Bitcoin prices shrink the cushion behind that collateral.

Buying more Bitcoin with cash during a downturn increases exposure to the same asset that secures the debt. If prices recover, the averaging-down looks smart in hindsight. If they keep sliding, the balance sheet carries more Bitcoin risk than it did a week ago.
With Tether now in firm control after buying out SoftBank, Twenty One Capital's capital decisions increasingly reflect the strategy of one of crypto's largest and most closely watched companies.

title: Twenty One Capital buys 172.25 Bitcoin, lifting holdings to roughly 43,841 BTC
